notes: Parts are unchanged from step 1: Uno, breadboard, pushbutton, 10K resistor and five jumper wires. Nothing was added or dropped.

Pull-down wiring: button side 1 (column 4) goes to 5V through the orange wire and the + rail. Button side 2 (column 6) goes to Uno pin 2 (teal wire) and to GND through the 10K resistor (column 6 to column 9) and the short black wire to the - rail. Pressing the button puts 5V on pin 2; releasing it leaves pin 2 at GND.

The breadboard image labels its top half rows j-f and its bottom half a-e. I used the catalogue naming instead: top half 't' (rows a-e) and bottom half 'b' (rows f-j). Column numbers and the electrical result are the same.
The button straddles the centre gap. Its two legs in column 4 form side 1 and its two legs in column 6 form side 2. I read the leg columns as 4 and 6 from the image.
The exact rail hole numbers (bp.2, bn.2, bp.4, bn.9) are approximate, read from the image. Each rail is a single strip, so the numbers do not change the electrical result.
The black wire from the Uno goes to the lower of the two GND pins on the power header, which I mapped to GND.2.
The built-in LED on pin 13 is on the Uno board, so it is not added as a separate part.
